candidates.title: Your Side Still Stays Yours
candidates.one_line_concept: Even when one partner is alone, they still do not spread into the other person's usual place, so the empty side becomes proof that the house is waiting for its real person.
candidates.emotional_truth: Missing someone is not always crying. Sometimes it is your body refusing to act like their place is available.
candidates.relatable_trigger: People who still leave their partner's side of the bed, sofa, table, or car untouched when the partner is away will feel caught.
candidates.visual_evidence: One partner sits on only their usual half of a sofa or bed; the other half is visibly empty, uncreased, and respected. No dramatic longing, just a body keeping the boundary out of habit.

suggested_slide_arc.slide_1: The locked lyric sits over a quiet frame where one half of a shared place is empty but not taken over.
suggested_slide_arc.slide_2: The note lands on the comfort that the empty side is not emptiness alone; it is a place still kept for the person who makes it ghar.
suggested_slide_arc.story_room_note: If a third slide is added later, it should be one more physical receipt of the kept place, not a moral explanation.

candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu or Zuv is alone on a shared sofa or bed, unconsciously staying on their own side while the other side remains open.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The empty side is reframed as loyalty, not loneliness: the house has room because the person still belongs there.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Send trigger: 'I literally still leave your side.' Comment trigger: people naming the place they never take over.
candidates.why_not_generic: The idea does not say home is a person; it shows the tiny bodily habit of reserving someone's place when nobody is watching.

top_pick.title: Your Side Still Stays Yours
top_pick.why_meera_picks_it: It has the smallest real behavior and the cleanest photographic proof. A stranger could say 'home is a person'; only someone who has missed their person keeps sitting on one half of a shared place when nobody is there to notice.
protect_this: the reserved side as the emotional receipt
slide 2 as a private note, not a lesson
absence that feels comforting because the person still belongs
top_pick.if_it_starts_feeling_flat: Make the body behavior more obvious before changing the copy: the alone partner must visibly avoid taking the other person's place.

rejected_patterns.why_rejected: It proves nothing except that a room is empty. The viewer needs a human receipt, not decor around a lyric.

rejected_patterns.pattern: Home is not a place, it is you
rejected_patterns.why_rejected: This is the known generic version. It explains the premise and gives the viewer no reason to send it except agreement.
Too easy, too stock, and it erases the more interesting ache before the person arrives.
The copy contract explicitly warns against making random objects lead the premise. Objects can prove the behavior, not become the hook.
Words like safety, grounding, attachment, and healing would flatten the song ache into a lesson.

risk_notes: The core theme already exists in the winner bank, so novelty must come from the Aachu/Zuv lived wrapper, not from smoother phrasing.
The creator requested two slides; do not expand unless the story room finds one genuinely necessary extra receipt.
Only the creator-provided lyric is allowed. No additional song lyrics should appear in any later slide, prompt, caption, or QA note.
The strongest candidates use absence, but absence must be readable as devotion and belonging, not abandonment or grief.
